To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amortized cost of finding a regular path between two given nodes in a graph isO(nk2), and the worst-case cost isO(l+|ℒ|), where l is the length of this path.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of data structures for the on-line dynamic ℒ-path problem and the design and analysis for the dynamic one-sided recursive query problem.

a new kind of data structure that supports dynamic insertion and deletion of edges, and dynamic queries about the presence of paths in the graph, where the paths are defined by a regular expression over the labels of the edges.

the following questions: How to build and maintain efficiently data structures that support on-line insertion and deletion operations on graphs, and how to exploit the structure of the data to answer efficiently queries about the graphs.

we present an algorithm for solving the dynamic ℒ-path problem inO(nk+1) time, which is optimal in the worst case, and that we show how this algorithm can be used to solve some recursive queries on knowledge bases in a relative time ofO(m/n).

, in some cases, the dynamic setting can be exploited to obtain improved time bounds for queries on dynamic graphs.
